test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Karad, which was recognised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs for achieving 100 % segregation, collection, and processing of sanitary and biomedical waste in April 2025, is located in which of the following districts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Satara district**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karad**, a prominent city in the state of **Maharashtra**, is located within the **Satara district**. It has gained significant national attention for its excellence in urban waste management.
 
• In **April 2025**, the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** officially recognized the city for achieving **100% segregation, collection, and processing** of both **sanitary** and **biomedical waste**.
 
• This milestone reflects the city's commitment to the **Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) 2.0**, which emphasizes making cities "Garbage Free" and ensuring the scientific processing of all categories of waste.
 
• The recognition highlights the successful implementation of decentralized waste processing models, where **biomedical waste** from hospitals and **sanitary waste** from households are handled without contaminating regular municipal solid waste. ***Hence, the correct answer is Satara district.***
 
• The city's administration utilized advanced tracking and specialized collection vehicles to ensure that no **hazardous waste** reaches the landfills, setting a benchmark for other **Grade-C** municipal councils in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Significance:**
 
 
• **Karad** is situated at the **confluence (Sangam)** of the **Krishna** and **Koyna** rivers. This confluence is locally known as **"Preeti Sangam"**, which translates to the "Confluence of Love."
 
• The city is located at an altitude of approximately **566 meters** and is a major educational and industrial hub in **Western Maharashtra**.
 
 
 
• **Satara District:**
 
 
• The district was the seat of the **Maratha Empire** in the **18th century** and served as the capital under **Chhatrapati Shahu I**.
 
• It is home to the famous **Kaas Plateau** (Valley of Flowers), which is a **UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site**.
 
 
 
• **Biomedical Waste Management:**
 
 
• Management of such waste is governed by the **Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016**, which require the segregation of waste into color-coded bags (**Yellow, Red, White, and Blue**) to prevent health risks.
 
• The achievement in **2025** signifies that **Karad** has successfully integrated these rules into its daily municipal operations.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other Options:**
 
 
• **Indore district** (Madhya Pradesh) is consistently ranked as **India's cleanest city** in the **Swachh Survekshan** but is distinct from the specific recognition given to **Karad**.
 
• **Coimbatore district** is located in **Tamil Nadu** and is known for its textile industry, while **Dehradun district** is the capital of **Uttarakhand**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Swachh Survekshan:** It is an annual survey of cleanliness, hygiene, and sanitation in villages, cities, and towns across **India**, launched as part of the **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** in **2016**.
 
• **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs:** This ministry is the nodal agency for the **Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)** and is headed by a **Union Cabinet Minister**.
 
• **Waste Segregation:** The **100% segregation** target involves separating **Wet waste (biodegradable)**, **Dry waste (recyclable)**, and **Domestic Hazardous waste** (including sanitary napkins and diapers) at the source.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** By processing **100% of biomedical waste**, **Karad** prevents the spread of infectious diseases and reduces the soil and groundwater pollution often caused by unscientific disposal.
